messages:
maria: heads up — a Dedicated tenant got routed to Hosted fallback during a regional surge. they are demanding strict isolation; said Dedicated must never spill to Hosted for them. is our behavior explicit in the API or just an implementation quirk?
liam: quick context: tenants can opt-out via tenant.spillover_allowed=false. if unset or true, routing considers cost+latency and will fall back to Hosted when Dedicated is exhausted.
sanjay: telemetry found ~12 tenants missing the opt-out flag; a few are large and expected isolation. ops has been manually toggling but we lack a reliable mapping from contract to tenant metadata.
taylor: console UX problem: onboarding doesn't prominently show "no spillover". product added a checkbox during contracting but it's easy to miss.
maria: can we detect this at runtime and reject instead of silently sending them to Hosted? customers expect a clear failure if they asked for isolation.
liam: there is a race now: request -> tenant lookup -> capacity check -> decision. we check tenant.spillover_allowed at lookup, but if the Dedicated pool is in a transient draining/evac state we may decide to fallback before a final lock is visible.
maria: show me sample logs for the incident.
liam: example:
```
2026-03-15T16:04:12Z routing: tenant=acme-corp id=2345 preferred=dedicated pool_state=draining tokens_allowed=0 -> fallback=hosted reason=evac
2026-03-15T16:04:12Z policy: tenant.spillover_allowed=true
```
maria: that tenant.spillover_allowed should have been false. if false we should either 1) reject with structured error or 2) queue until Dedicated recovers. product expects reject + clear error code.
taylor: product asks for three things: (a) explicit machine-readable routing header in API responses, (b) console banner for strict isolation tenants, (c) a dashboard metric + alert when strict tenants hit capacity.
sanjay: propose metrics: spillover_attempt_total, spillover_rejected_total, spillover_accepted_total. tag by region, tenant_tier, model_security. add fallback_reason label.
liam: internal debate: should we return X-Redwood-Route: dedicated|hosted|rejected? and a X-Redwood-Route-Reason header like isolation_opt_out|capacity_evacuated|tenant_quota? I'm in favor so downstream proxies and customer SDKs can react.
maria: absolutely. plus a clear HTTP status for rejected strict tenants. what status? 423 Locked or 409 Conflict?
sanjay: semantically 423 fits our eviction/lock patterns, but make sure we also include a machine error code in the body: {"code":"DEDICATED_UNAVAILABLE","can_retry":false}. SDKs can map that.
liam: implementation sketch: on routing lookup: if tenant.spillover_allowed == false and not dedicated_pool.available_for(tenant): return 423 with X-Redwood-Route: rejected and X-Redwood-Route-Reason: dedicated_unavailable_isolation
maria: also require tracing: emit a tenant.audit entry with last_5_routing_decisions to aid postmortems.
taylor: console UX: show banner "Isolation: Strict — Hosted fallback disabled" with link to docs, show "Last attempted spillover" timestamp, and quick "Request more capacity" button that opens a provisioning ticket.
ops-bot: alert: tenant=2345 attempted hosted fallback -> isolation_violation (rule: tenant.spillover_allowed=false)
sanjay: automations: if strict tenant hits capacity >3 times in 1h, auto-open a P1 ticket. tag region and attach recent routing decisions.
liam: edge case: model-scoped isolation — some tenants only need privacy for certain models (private weights). product wants a per-model override (tenant default + model flag). that impacts cache keys and routing key: tenant_id + model_security_profile.
maria: that will increase complexity for routing cache invalidation. make sure we version the routing cache key and invalidate on metadata change.
sanjay: telemetry tweak: add model_security=public|private label and count model-level spillovers. that will help ops prioritize reprovisioning.
liam: small integration test plan: simulate Dedicated pool drain and assert we return 423 + X-Redwood-Route headers for strict tenants; assert Hosted routing for permissive tenants. add unit tests for header presence.
maria: next steps summary: 
- liam: add X-Redwood-Route & X-Redwood-Route-Reason headers; return structured 423 for strict rejections (ETA: 2 sprints)
- sanjay: add metrics, fallback_reason tag, tenant audit last_5_decisions, and dashboard tile for strict tenant spillovers (ETA: 1 sprint)
- taylor: console: Isolation banner, last attempted spillover, request capacity button (ETA: 2 sprints)
- maria/product: update onboarding checklist so contract "no spillover" toggles tenant.spillover_allowed (you own this)
liam: ops integration: create support ticket if strict tenant spillover_attempts >3 in 1h; enterprise tenants also trigger pager.
maria: any objections?
liam: none here.
sanjay: lgtm.
taylor: lgtm :thumbsup:
ops-bot: created ticket #INC-2026: dedicated-spillover-isolation-violation -> assigned to liam, priority=high
maria: thanks — I'll track RFC and follow up once dashboards + headers are live.
